Visit note | 2025-06-18 11:30 AM | Dr. Ishrat Jahan, Psychiatry | Patient: Abdul Molla, 44, male. Mr. Molla describes experiencing recurrent panic attacks characterized by a terrifying fear of dying, breathlessness, and normal heart test results. Notably, he mentions having attacks that wake the patient from sleep. These episodes began after a traffic accident in Badda, and he works as a security guard. He reports having about 9 panic attacks in the last month. He has no relevant comorbidity. He denies depressed mood, persistent sadness, or suicidal thoughts. On examination: BP 121/71 mmHg, pulse 86 bpm, weight 93 kg. Mental state examination shows normal mood and affect, though he appears anxious when discussing the attacks. Assessment: Panic disorder. Plan: a prescription was issued today. He was advised to practise slow breathing during attacks, reduce caffeine intake, and start counselling sessions. Follow-up in 4 weeks.
